newsitem.title: MONACO: SWIMMING-CHINESE SPRINTERS SHINE IN MONACO.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-CHINESE SPRINTERS SHINE IN MONACO.

text.p: Chinese sprinters collected four wins and Russia prevailed in seven events on the second day of a low-key two-day Monaco international swimming meeting on Sunday.

Shan Ying and Nian Yun, who shared in two world record breaking Chinese women's freestyle relays at last month's world short-course championships in Sweden, completed a one-two in the women's 100 metres freestyle.
Shan, seventh in the 1996 Olympic 50 freestyle final, won in 56.59 seconds, with Nian second in 56.80. But both were well outside the 54.01 world mark of their Chinese compatriot Le Jingyi.

Cai Huijue, who lowered the women's 50 butterfly world best mark to 27.26 on Saturday, won the final head-to-head with Russia's Natalia Meshcheryakova on Sunday in 27.29 -- outside her new world standard but once again faster than the previous mark of 27.30 set by Qian Hong in Perth, Australia, in January 1991.
There were further Chinese wins for Jiang Chengli in the men's 50 freestyle and Han Xue in the women's 50 breaststroke.
Russia, whose double Olympic butterfly champion Denis Pankratov pulled out because of an ailment, led the way with seven wins on the second day.

Olga Kochetkov won the women's 50 and 100 backstroke and European champion Vladimir Selkov turned the tables on Saturday's 100 backstroke victor Volodymir Nikolaychuk of the Ukraine by winning Sunday's 200 event.

The other Russian winners on Sunday were Vladimir Pyshnenko (men's 200 freestyle), Roman Ivanovsky (men's 100 breaststroke), Stanislav Lopukhov (men's 50 breaststroke) and Meshcheryakova (women's 50 freestyle).

On Saturday, Germany's Sandra Voelker, double Olympic freestyle medallist at the Atlanta Games, set a world mark for the 50 metres backstroke of 29.00 seconds, breaking the 29.05 set by China's Yang Wenyi in Tokyo in August 1989.
